body: Looks like quite a big jump in the Docker API - from minimum version `1.24 `to `1.44`. Our Testcontainers setup reports: > Client version 1.32 is too old. Minimum supported API version is 1.44. Please upgrade your client to a newer version. ```bash podman run --rm --privileged -it docker:28-dind # vs podman run --rm --privileged -it docker:29-dind ``` `docker:29-dind` was released `Nov 11, 2025 at 7:08 am` (4h ago by writing this) https://hub.docker.com/_/docker/tags?name=-dind
Apparently docker is requiring now minimum `1.44` API version, so TC is not working anymore unless we override the api version via ENV variables or docker-java.properties in the project.

Workaround is to set the client version explicitly.
For instance in $HOME/.docker-java.properties

`api.version=1.44`

First of all, thank you testcontainers contributors for your continuous contribution!

Today I have faced the same issue, and solved it by setting `api.version` system property.
Probably the root cause of this issue is here; testcontainers-java sets docker remote API version explicitly in case of no API version is set via [configurations](https://github.com/docker-java/docker-java/blob/cbf88f5a6d3407159c69fd0ffc715a6ff4d11ef8/docs/getting_started.md#instantiating-a-dockerclientconfig).

https://github.com/testcontainers/testcontainers-java/blob/73726f436fb469469986866ab55f67057d0beba4/core/src/main/java/org/testcontainers/dockerclient/DockerClientProviderStrategy.java#L406-L408

I guess that we can change these lines to use `VERSION_1_44` by default, or simply remove these lines to let docker-java negotiates proper version with docker server. But I'm not so sure why we set the version explicitly here, so we may need other changes to solve this issue.

Hi folks, we are aware of this issue and will provide workarounds and a fix shortly.
